title: Morning Robotics Scan
report:
## RAPID: Robot Agentic Programming from Demonstrations

### The Breakthrough
RAPID automatically generates, verifies, and refines robot programs from a single visual human demonstration. It infers an object‑centric relational program and uses trajectory‑optimization primitives that adapt to scene geometry at run time, enabling reuse across eight contact‑rich tasks, LIBERO‑Pro benchmarks, and a real Franka arm with pose, shape, material, and environment generalization.

### The Caveats
The paper reports improvements without comparing against any existing baselines, so it’s unclear whether RAPID actually outperforms prior methods.

## Self-Adaptive VLA for Robust Robot Deployment

### The Breakthrough
A post‑training recipe lets Vision‑Language‑Action models self‑adapt during deployment by injecting hardware shifts, creating shift‑conditioned expert demos, and adding a lightweight context encoder with adaptive layer‑norm; this restores over 80% of the base policy’s performance under actuation bias and encoder offsets on four bi‑manual and dexterous manipulation tasks.

### The Caveats
The paper evaluates only against the non‑adaptive VLA baseline and does not compare to any existing adaptation or calibration methods.

## Capability-Tradeoff Contact Selection (CTCS) for Legged Loco‑Manipulation

### The Breakthrough
CTCS screens and groups candidate contacts, predicts their capabilities via local sensitivity analysis, and performs selective exact evaluations, achieving roughly 3× planning speedup while preserving task quality on a Unitree Go2 quadruped with an AgileX NERO arm, outperforming ground‑only and fixed‑contact baselines.

### The Caveats
The method is validated only on a single quadruped‑arm platform and nine support surfaces.

## Rolling‑WAM: Faster Closed‑Loop Manipulation via Rolling Imagination

### The Breakthrough
A sliding‑window rolling noise schedule fully denoises the imminent action chunk while partially refining future chunks, eliminating full‑horizon denoising each cycle and delivering a 4.5× replanning speedup with comparable success on LIBERO, RoboTwin, and a real Unitree G1 humanoid.

### The Caveats
The speedup is shown only on those benchmarks and a single robot, leaving broader applicability unproven.

## Agentic CUDA Kernel Optimizer

### The Breakthrough
The tool stitches a C++ harness, CUDA execution, and Nsight profiling under AI‑agent control, enabling prompts to drive kernel selection, execution, and benchmark reporting in an end‑to‑end pipeline.

### The Caveats
The demo provides only a handcrafted harness with no quantitative results, hardware diversity, or comparison to existing CUDA optimization tools.

## osprey: Agentic interface and safety harness for scientific control systems

### The Breakthrough
Osprey adds an agentic orchestration layer that decomposes operator requests into auditable steps, inserts mandatory human‑approval gates, and checks channel boundaries before any hardware write, supporting protocol‑agnostic connectors for large facilities.

### The Caveats
The repository provides no formal evaluation or baseline comparison, so its safety‑gate and human‑in‑the‑loop claims remain unvalidated.

## OpenHarness: unified, encrypted command center for multiple AI coding agents

### The Breakthrough
OpenHarness runs a per‑machine daemon that launches agents in real tmux panes and streams text over ChaCha20‑Poly1305‑encrypted WebRTC channels with automatic path selection, achieving 11–13 ms median latency and ~0.1 % CPU core usage.

### The Caveats
The latency and resource use claims are unsubstantiated; no comparison to existing remote‑development solutions is provided.

### Priority
RAPID offers a concrete path to turn single‑demo teaching into reusable robot programs, directly accelerating prototyping and deployment for a wide range of manipulation tasks.

### One action
Visit the RAPID paper and repository, and try reproducing the Franka arm demo on your own hardware to evaluate its generalization potential.
